title: Mission Fatigue
doc: CKF Hard Mode - mission fatigue.
A THREE-TIER TRACK. Every merc who completes a mission rolls once. A merc
who fails the roll moves up one tier from the highest tier they already
carry: nothing to tier 1, tier 1 to tier 2, tier 2 to tier 3. A merc
already carrying tier 3 is not rolled, because there is nowhere above it.
The trait granted at each tier is tier1.traitId, tier2.traitId and
tier3.traitId (Fatigue.Resolve, Fatigue.Apply).
ONE ROLL FOR EVERY TIER. Moving up is not automatic - the same roll against
the same chancePercent, with the same Wound Resist subtracted from it,
decides a first grant and a move to tier 2 or tier 3 alike
(Fatigue.ThresholdFor). There is one chance curve and one duration curve,
and both apply at every tier.
TRAITS STACK. Moving up a tier does not remove the tier below it. All three
shipped fatigue traits are TraitClass 6 in their own TraitGroup, so one
merc can carry several at once and their penalties apply together. Each row
expires on its own schedule, counted from the mission that granted it, so
the lower tiers lapse first (Fatigue.Apply).
ONE POOL, ONE CLAMP. Everybody eligible to roll is in one pool, whatever
tier they are on, and minAffected and maxAffected bound the TOTAL number of
grants the mission makes. A floor can therefore force a move up a tier, and
a ceiling can spare one; both reach for the mercs whose roll landed nearest
their own threshold (Fatigue.Clamp).
THIS SUBSYSTEM WRITES TO YOUR SAVE. It inserts GameCharacterTrait rows,
which the game's own SaveManager.ProcessTraits expires on schedule. No new
table, no new column, no side file and no tick of its own, so uninstalling
the mod leaves at most a few live traits, which lapse by themselves
(Fatigue.Apply).
A LOST mission costs nothing. The game writes no score row of any kind on
defeat, so the hook never fires there (Fatigue.AfterInsertGameScore).
SOLO MISSIONS ARE EXEMPT. A mission whose roster is one character runs none
of this: no roll, nothing written (Fatigue.Resolve).
THE 4.0 LAYOUT IS RETIRED. runningEmpty and offDuty were two blocks with
four byPowerLevel curves between them, and escalation to Off-Duty was
unconditional. Both blocks still PARSE so that a 4.0 file loads instead of
being refused for keys that map to no member, and a file carrying one gets a
log line naming it, but nothing reads them. Their curves do not stand behind
the two below (Fatigue.LegacyKeys).
A mission whose PowerLevel cannot be read takes the LOWEST ANCHOR of each
curve, which makes a one-anchor PL 1 curve behave like a flat value. A
once-only warning says so.
uiDoc: Missions tire the crew. Every merc who finishes one rolls once, and a merc who fails moves up one step: first to the tier 1 trait, then tier 2, then tier 3. Moving up needs the same roll as the first grant, so nothing escalates on its own. A mission you lose costs nothing because this only fires on a win, and a merc who goes out alone is exempt.
The steps stack rather than replace: a merc on tier 2 is still carrying tier 1, and both sets of penalties apply until each one runs out. The lower step always expires first.

One odds and duration table covers all three steps, and the Cyber Knight can have his own. The floor and the ceiling count every grant a mission makes, at any step, so a floor can push someone up a step and a ceiling can spare them.

Wound Resist is subtracted from a merc's chance, one point of resist per percentage point. Most cyberware carries negative Wound Resist, so a heavily chromed crew typically tires faster than a clean one. The safehouse's built modules, a merc's traits, their character effects, their implants and their armour all count towards resist.
Leave the rolls deterministic unless you want fatigue to be rerollable: with it on, reloading the victory screen gives the same outcome every time.

fields.label: Enable Mission Fatigue
fields.doc: Slice toggle. It lives in ckf.hardmode.cfg because a gate cannot live inside the file it gates, and the .cfg is parsed before anything else loads. Slices.Init binds every [Slices] key above the [General] Enabled bail-out, so BepInEx writes the line even when the mod is off. A key that cannot be read is reported at Error and treated as on. Off: the subsystem logs why and does nothing this launch. The retired "enabled" key inside the subsystem's JSON file is still parsed (RetiredEnabled) so that Slices.ReportRetiredGate can report it: a Warning, or an Error when it is false and this key is not. Nothing branches on it.
fields.uiDoc: Turn this off and this part of the mod does nothing; the game uses its own values. The master switch on the first page turns off everything at once.

fields.label: Odds and duration by power level
fields.uiDoc: One table for all three tiers. Scale the chance, the duration, the floor and the ceiling. Values between anchors interpolate, and below the lowest and above the highest the nearest anchor holds. Two anchors describe all twenty levels, listing all twenty works identically if you would rather set each one by hand, and a single anchor at power level 1 is how you write a flat value. Each field interpolates over only the anchors that name it. chancePercent is per merc, per completed mission, and Wound Resist is subtracted from it before the roll; the same number decides a first grant and a move up a tier. durationDays must be at least 1 because 0 makes the trait permanent, and it is the length of whichever tier the merc was granted. minAffected is a floor on how many mercs are granted a tier on this mission: it moves the count only, the rolls still decide who, and it is capped at the number of mercs eligible to roll. maxAffected is the ceiling and must not sit below the floor at any level.
fields.doc: Anchor points that scale chancePercent, durationDays, minAffected and maxAffected with the mission's PowerLevel - the effective level, the one [PowerLevel] lifts past the stock ceiling of 10, read from GameMissionModel.PowerLevel and NOT from PowerLevelUnscaled (Fatigue.ReadPowerLevel). Elapse's identically shaped byPowerLevel tables key on PowerLevelUnscaled instead; the two subsystems read different columns. Values between anchors interpolate; below the lowest and above the highest the nearest anchor holds, because a curve is a statement about the levels it names rather than an extrapolation past them (Fatigue.Curve). Two anchors describe all twenty levels, listing all twenty works identically, and a single anchor is a flat value written as a curve. ONE CURVE SERVES ALL THREE TIERS: the chance that grants tier 1 is the chance that moves a merc to tier 2 or tier 3, and the duration written on a tier-3 row is the duration written on a tier-1 row. This table is the only place these four numbers live, so nothing stands behind a field no anchor names: Fatigue returns 'no value' and the roll or the write that needed it does not happen and is logged, except minAffected, whose absence means no floor and is a warning rather than an error (Fatigue.ChanceFor, Fatigue.DaysFor, Fatigue.MinAffectedFor, Fatigue.MaxAffectedFor). Per-anchor validation: chancePercent 0-100, durationDays at least 1 because a zero-turn ExpiresTurn is how the game marks a trait PERMANENT, counts not negative, and a PL 1-20 sweep rejecting a ceiling that drops below the floor at any level (Fatigue.CheckLevels, Fatigue.Validate). NOTE ON SHAPE: this block is a JSON object whose KEYS are the power levels, and each value is one anchor; 'powerLevel' below is that key, not a member of the anchor object. A key outside 1-20 is warned about and still used.
fields.absent: REFUSED while fatigue is enabled. A mission whose PowerLevel cannot be read is NOT this case - it takes the lowest anchor of each curve, and is warned about once.

fields.label: Cyber Knight odds and duration by power level
fields.uiDoc: The Cyber Knight can have his own odds and duration, across all three tiers, but is bound to the general floor and ceiling like everyone else. Wherever this curve has no value, the CK is treated as any other merc.
fields.doc: The Cyber Knight's own curve, shaped like byPowerLevel and keyed on the same effective PowerLevel. Where it names a value the Knight uses it; where it does not, the general curve is used (Fatigue.ChanceFor, Fatigue.DaysFor). It carries chancePercent and durationDays only: the Knight sits inside the general minAffected and maxAffected clamp (David's rule), so a floor or a ceiling here would have nothing to act on. Optional.
fields.absent: The Cyber Knight rolls on the general byPowerLevel curve and takes its duration, exactly like any other merc.

fields.label: Tier 1 trait id
fields.uiDoc: The trait granted to a merc carrying no fatigue who fails the roll. 2007 Checked Out is the mildest of the three shipped fatigue traits.
fields.doc: The trait granted to a merc carrying none of the three who fails the roll. 2007 Checked Out is the default. All three tiers must name a different id, none may be 0 or negative, and none may land in the range this project reserves for RowClone's constructed rows (Fatigue.Validate). The id is written straight into GameCharacterTraitModel.TraitTypeId with no lookup, and it is NOT checked against the content database - see the note in Fatigue.Validate for what that does and does not catch.

fields.label: Tier 2 trait id
fields.uiDoc: The trait granted to a merc already carrying tier 1 who fails the roll. 2009 Running Empty is the default. The tier 1 trait stays on them as well.
fields.doc: The trait granted to a merc already carrying tier1.traitId who fails the roll. 2009 Running Empty is the default; its effect row's locale name is "Bloodless". The tier 1 row is NOT removed - the tiers stack and each expires on its own schedule (Fatigue.Resolve). Must differ from the other two tiers.

fields.label: Tier 3 trait id
fields.uiDoc: The trait granted to a merc already carrying tier 2 who fails the roll. 2014 Off-Duty is the default, and the game keeps an Off-Duty merc off the roster until it expires. A merc already on tier 3 is not rolled again.
fields.doc: The trait granted to a merc already carrying tier2.traitId who fails the roll, and the top of the track: a merc carrying it is not rolled, because there is no tier above it (Fatigue.Resolve). 2014 Off-Duty is the default. Keeping an Off-Duty merc off the roster is the ENGINE'S job and runs off that trait's SpecialCode 90 BlockMissions; the mod grants the trait and stops there - it deliberately does not filter ReadGameCharactersAvailableForMission, which is what leaves the game's own 'unless required by mission' story override intact, so an Off-Duty merc can still be pulled into a mission that requires them. Must differ from the other two tiers.

fields.label: Wound Resist mitigation
fields.uiDoc: Subtract a merc's Wound Resist from their chance. Positive resist protects; negative resist makes fatigue more likely, and most cyberware is negative, so a chromed crew tires faster. Off, and every merc rolls the base chance.
fields.doc: Subtract a merc's Wound Resist from their chance, one point per percentage point, at every tier. Positive resist protects; negative resist makes fatigue more likely, and most cyberware is negative - 51 of the 83 implants that carry Wound Resist [measured]. A crew whose implants sum to -10 to -39 turns a 25% base into 35-64%; that is deliberate, and chrome making you tire faster is the point (Fatigue.ResistFor). What counts: the safehouse's built modules (a Triage Clinic grants WoundRes 10/15/20/30 by upgrade level, re-read once per mission so an upgrade takes effect mid-session - Fatigue.SafehouseResist), the merc's traits, their character effects, their implants, their job nodes and their armour. Job nodes are read for completeness and contribute nothing: 0 of the 1,525 JobNodeModel rows in the game data point at an effect carrying Wound Resist. Armour (David's rule) is the merc's armour row from ReadGameArmorByCharacter, its own effect plus any crafted upgrade, and any ArmorEffect (classification 9) arriving through another reader, counted once. Armour is the only reliably positive source, so it offsets the cyberware penalty; the roll line reports it as gear. False and every merc rolls the base chance.

fields.label: Minimum chance after resist
fields.doc: The chance never falls below this however much resist a merc carries, so nobody is fully immune and minAffected always has someone to reach for. Set it to 0 to let resist cancel a chance outright. It bounds what RESIST takes away and never raises a chance already at or below it, so a configured chance of 0 still means no roll (Fatigue.ThresholdFor).

fields.label: Deterministic rolls
fields.doc: Seed each roll from (mission turn, character id) so reloading the victory screen reproduces the same outcome. False makes the roll unseeded, which lets you reroll on save or load.

fields.label: Log grants
fields.doc: One line per grant in the BepInEx log, naming the tier the merc moved to and the tiers they were already carrying. Nothing about this feature is verifiable without it.
